## Confounders
Based on prior literature and biological plausibility, we selected the following as confounders:
-Age
-Sex
-Socioeconomic status (SEIFA disadvantge index, income decile)
-Smoking status
-Education/qualification level
-alcohol level
-energy levels

Rosetta (main model):

The [model script](rq3-rosetta-main.R), [methods and formatted results](rq3-rosetta-methods-results.md), and four aggregate CSV tables are in this repository. The primary interaction estimates are shown below; the methods file explains the sample restrictions and survey weights.

| Sample | Complete cases | Adjusted fibre × PA interaction OR (95% CI) | p-value |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| General NNPAS | 3,960 | 0.97 (0.86–1.09) | 0.559 |
| Indigenous NATSINPAS | 408 | 0.79 (0.54–1.16) | 0.232 |

Neither analysis shows clear evidence of physical-activity modification. NNPAS is a general-population sample, not a verified non-Indigenous sample; these cleaned files include ages 18–65 and the Indigenous activity sample is non-remote.

General (Non-indigenous):
Boxplot of bmi, waist, fibre
```{r}
check_outliers <- function(data, name) {
  boxplot(data$bmi, main = paste(name, "- BMI"))
  boxplot(data$waist_cm, main = paste(name, "- Waist Circumference"))
  boxplot(data$fibre_2day_avg_g, main = paste(name, "- Fibre Intake"))
}

check_outliers(general, "General")
check_outliers(indigenous, "Indigenous")
```

Missing data check:
```{r}
check_missing <- function(data, name) {
  cat("Missingness for", name, ":\n")
  print(colSums(is.na(data)))
  cat("\n")
}

check_missing(general, "General")
check_missing(indigenous, "Indigenous")
```
